The Meridian Method

A clear path from where you are to where you want to be.

STEP 01 / 04 Discover
01 02 03 04
  1. 01Step 01 of 04

    Discover

    It starts with a conversation.

    Before recommending anything, I want to understand you.

    We’ll talk about your goals, training history, lifestyle, schedule, nutrition, previous successes and struggles, and most importantly, what has prevented you from getting where you want to go on your own.

    This isn’t a high-pressure sales pitch. It’s an opportunity for us to determine what you actually need and whether Meridian Performance is the right fit to help you get there.

  2. 02Step 02 of 04

    Assess

    Understand the starting point.

    If we’re meeting in person, we’ll establish objective baselines through tools such as body-composition measurements and a movement assessment.

    We’ll look at how you move, where you’re strong, where limitations exist, and what your current fitness level looks like.

    Instead of guessing what you need, we establish a starting point we can build from.

  3. 03Step 03 of 04

    Build

    Create your roadmap.

    Once we understand where you are and where you want to go, we build the system around you.

    That can include your personalized training plan, nutrition targets and habits, weekly schedule, accountability structure, progress metrics, and resources to make execution easier in the real world.

    The goal isn’t to create the theoretically perfect plan.

    It’s to create the best plan you can consistently follow.

  4. 04Step 04 of 04

    Coach, Measure & Adjust

    Execution is where coaching actually begins.

    From your first training session forward, we’ll work through the plan together while tracking progress and making adjustments based on your results.

    You’ll learn proper technique, understand why you’re doing what you’re doing, develop confidence in the gym, and receive consistent accountability outside of it.

    Through regular check-ins, progress reviews, and ongoing communication, we continue asking:

    • What’s working?
    • What’s not?
    • What needs to change?

    Your program evolves as you do.
